sanskrit: adharmeṇa samāyukto yamasya viṣayaṃ gataḥ mahad duḥkhaṃ samāsādya tiryagyonau prajāyate
english: Bound to unrighteousness, he passes into the realm of Yama; and having undergone immense suffering there, he is reborn into the womb of a beast.

sanskrit: karmaṇā yena yeneha yasyāṃ yonau prajāyate jīvo mohasamāyuktas tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: By which particular deed, and in which womb, the deluded living being is reborn here—hear that now from me as I declare it.

sanskrit: yad etad ucyate śāstre setihāse sacchandasi yamasya viṣayaṃ ghoraṃ martyo lokaḥ prapadyate
english: What is taught in the scriptures, together with the legends and the sacred meters: the mortal world enters the dreadful realm of Yama.

sanskrit: adhītya caturo vedān dvijo mohasamanvitaḥ patitāt pratigṛhyātha kharayonau prajāyate
english: A twice-born who has studied the four Vedas, yet who, possessed by delusion, accepts a gift from a fallen man, is reborn thereafter into the womb of an ass.

sanskrit: kharo jīvati varṣāṇi daśa pañca ca bhārata kharo mṛto balīvardaḥ sapta varṣāṇi jīvati
english: As an ass he lives fifteen years, O Bhārata; and the ass, once dead, lives on as an ox for seven years.

sanskrit: balīvardo mṛtaś cāpi jāyate brahmarākṣasaḥ brahmarakṣas tu trīn māsāṃs tato jāyati brāhmaṇaḥ
english: And the ox, when it too has died, is born as a brahma-rākṣasa; as a brahma-rākṣasa for three months, and after that he is born a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: patitaṃ yājayitvā tu kṛmiyonau prajāyate tatra jīvati varṣāṇi daśa pañca ca bhārata
english: But one who has performed sacrifices for a fallen man is reborn into the womb of a worm; there he lives fifteen years, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kṛmibhāvāt pramuktas tu tato jāyati gardabhaḥ gardabhaḥ pañca varṣāṇi pañca varṣāṇi sūkaraḥ śvā varṣam ekaṃ bhavati tato jāyati mānavaḥ
english: Released from the condition of a worm, he is then born a donkey; as a donkey for five years, as a boar for five years, and he becomes a dog for one year—after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: upādhyāyasya yaḥ pāpaṃ śiṣyaḥ kuryād abuddhimān sa jīva iha saṃsārāṃs trīn āpnoti na saṃśayaḥ
english: A foolish pupil who does evil to his teacher—that soul, beyond all doubt, attains here three rounds of transmigration.

sanskrit: prāk śvā bhavati rājendra tataḥ kravyāt tataḥ kharaḥ tataḥ pretaḥ parikliṣṭaḥ paścāj jāyati brāhmaṇaḥ
english: First he becomes a dog, O lord of kings, then a flesh-eating beast, then an ass; then a tormented hungry ghost, and afterwards he is born a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: manasāpi guror bhāryāṃ yaḥ śiṣyo yāti pāpakṛt so 'dhamān yāti saṃsārān adharmeṇeha cetasā
english: A sinful pupil who approaches his teacher's wife even in his mind—he, through that unrighteous intent, passes here into the basest rounds of rebirth.

sanskrit: śvayonau tu sa saṃbhūtas trīṇi varṣāṇi jīvati tatrāpi nidhanaṃ prāptaḥ kṛmiyonau prajāyate
english: Born in the womb of a dog, he lives three years; and meeting his death there too, he is reborn into the womb of a worm.

sanskrit: kṛmibhāvam anuprāpto varṣam ekaṃ sa jīvati tatas tu nidhanaṃ prāpya brahmayonau prajāyate
english: Having attained the state of a worm, he lives one year; and meeting his death thereafter, he is reborn into the womb of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: yadi putrasamaṃ śiṣyaṃ gurur hanyād akāraṇe ātmanaḥ kāmakāreṇa so 'pi haṃsaḥ prajāyate
english: If a teacher, without cause and at his own willful whim, should slay a pupil who is like a son to him, he too is reborn as a goose.

sanskrit: pitaraṃ mātaraṃ vāpi yas tu putro 'vamanyate so 'pi rājan mṛto jantuḥ pūrvaṃ jāyati gardabhaḥ
english: And a son who despises his father or his mother—that creature too, O king, when dead, is first born a donkey.

sanskrit: kharo jīvati māsāṃs tu daśa śvā ca caturdaśa biḍālaḥ sapta māsāṃs tu tato jāyati mānavaḥ
english: As an ass he lives ten months, as a dog fourteen, and as a cat seven months; after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: mātāpitaram ākruśya sārikaḥ saṃprajāyate tāḍayitvā tu tāv eva jāyate kacchapo nṛpa
english: Having reviled mother and father, one is born a mynah bird; and having struck those very two, he is born a tortoise, O king.

sanskrit: kacchapo daśa varṣāṇi trīṇi varṣāṇi śalyakaḥ vyālo bhūtvā tu ṣaṇ māsāṃs tato jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: As a tortoise ten years, as a porcupine three years; and having been a serpent for six months, after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: bhartṛpiṇḍam upāśnan yo rājadviṣṭāni sevate so 'pi mohasamāpanno mṛto jāyati vānaraḥ
english: He who, while eating his master's bread, serves the king's enemies—that man too, sunk in delusion, when dead is born a monkey.

sanskrit: vānaro daśa varṣāṇi trīṇi varṣāṇi mūṣakaḥ śvā bhūtvā cātha ṣaṇ māsāṃs tato jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: As a monkey ten years, as a rat three years; and having been a dog for six months, after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: nyāsāpahartā tu naro yamasya viṣayaṃ gataḥ saṃsārāṇāṃ śataṃ gatvā kṛmiyonau prajāyate
english: But a man who steals a deposit entrusted to him passes into the realm of Yama; having gone through a hundred rounds of rebirth, he is reborn into the womb of a worm.

sanskrit: tatra jīvati varṣāṇi daśa pañca ca bhārata duṣkṛtasya kṣayaṃ gatvā tato jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: There he lives fifteen years, O Bhārata; and once his evil deed is exhausted, after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: asūyako naraś cāpi mṛto jāyati śārṅgakaḥ viśvāsahartā tu naro mīno jāyati durmatiḥ
english: A spiteful, envious man, when dead, is born a śārṅgaka bird; and the betrayer of trust, that evil-minded man, is born a fish.

sanskrit: bhūtvā mīno 'ṣṭa varṣāṇi mṛgo jāyati bhārata mṛgas tu caturo māsāṃs tataś chāgaḥ prajāyate
english: Having been a fish for eight years, he is born a deer, O Bhārata; and as a deer for four months, after that he is born a goat.

sanskrit: chāgas tu nidhanaṃ prāpya pūrṇe saṃvatsare tataḥ kīṭaḥ saṃjāyate jantus tato jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: And the goat, meeting its death at the close of a full year, is then born as an insect; that creature thereafter is born a man.

sanskrit: dhānyān yavāṃs tilān māṣān kulatthān sarṣapāṃś caṇān kalāyān atha mudgāṃś ca godhūmān atasīs tathā
english: Grains, barley, sesame, black gram, horse-gram, mustard, chickpeas, peas, green gram, wheat, and linseed too—

sanskrit: sasyasyānyasya hartā ca mohāj jantur acetanaḥ sa jāyate mahārāja mūṣako nirapatrapaḥ
english: the thieving creature who, witless through delusion, steals these or any other crop—he is born, O great king, as a shameless rat.

sanskrit: tataḥ pretya mahārāja punar jāyati sūkaraḥ sūkaro jātamātras tu rogeṇa mriyate nṛpa
english: Then, having died, O great king, he is born again as a boar; and the boar, just newly born, dies of disease, O king.

sanskrit: śvā tato jāyate mūḍhaḥ karmaṇā tena pārthiva śvā bhūtvā pañca varṣāṇi tato jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: By that deed the deluded soul is then born a dog, O lord of the earth; and having been a dog for five years, after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: paradārābhimarśaṃ tu kṛtvā jāyati vai vṛkaḥ śvā sṛgālas tato gṛdhro vyālaḥ kaṅko bakas tathā
english: Having laid hands upon another's wife, one is indeed born a wolf; then a dog, a jackal, a vulture, a serpent, a heron, and likewise a crane.

sanskrit: bhrātur bhāryāṃ tu durbuddhir yo dharṣayati mohitaḥ puṃskokilatvam āpnoti so 'pi saṃvatsaraṃ nṛpa
english: The evil-minded man who, deluded, violates his brother's wife attains the state of a male cuckoo, and that for a full year, O king.

sanskrit: sakhibhāryāṃ guror bhāryāṃ rājabhāryāṃ tathaiva ca pradharṣayitvā kāmād yo mṛto jāyati sūkaraḥ
english: He who out of lust violates a friend's wife, his teacher's wife, or likewise the king's wife, when dead is born a boar.

sanskrit: sūkaraḥ pañca varṣāṇi pañca varṣāṇi śvāvidhaḥ pipīlakas tu ṣaṇ māsān kīṭaḥ syān māsam eva ca etān āsādya saṃsārān kṛmiyonau prajāyate
english: As a boar five years, as a porcupine five years, as an ant six months, and as an insect but a single month; having passed through these rebirths, he is reborn into the womb of a worm.

sanskrit: tatra jīvati māsāṃs tu kṛmiyonau trayodaśa tato 'dharmakṣayaṃ kṛtvā punar jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: There in the worm's womb he lives thirteen months; and having then worked off his unrighteousness, he is born a man once more.

sanskrit: upasthite vivāhe tu dāne yajñe 'pi vābhibho mohāt karoti yo vighnaṃ sa mṛto jāyate kṛmiḥ
english: When a wedding, a gift-giving, or a sacrifice is at hand, O lord, he who out of delusion raises an obstruction to it is born, when dead, a worm.

sanskrit: kṛmir jīvati varṣāṇi daśa pañca ca bhārata adharmasya kṣayaṃ kṛtvā tato jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: As a worm he lives fifteen years, O Bhārata; and having worked off his unrighteousness, after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ dattvā tu yaḥ kanyāṃ dvitīye saṃprayacchati so 'pi rājan mṛto jantuḥ kṛmiyonau prajāyate
english: He who, having first given his daughter in marriage, then bestows her upon a second suitor—that creature too, O king, when dead, is reborn into the womb of a worm.

sanskrit: tatra jīvati varṣāṇi trayodaśa yudhiṣṭhira adharmasaṃkṣaye yuktas tato jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: There he lives thirteen years, O Yudhiṣṭhira; and when his unrighteousness is fully spent, after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: devakāryam upākṛtya pitṛkāryam athāpi ca anirvāpya samaśnan vai tato jāyati vāyasaḥ
english: He who, having begun the rite for the gods and likewise the rite for the ancestors, eats his meal without first making the offerings—after that he is born a crow.

sanskrit: vāyaso daśa varṣāṇi tato jāyati kukkuṭaḥ jāyate lavakaś cāpi māsaṃ tasmāt tu mānuṣaḥ
english: As a crow ten years, then he is born a cock; he is born too a quail for a month, and from that he becomes a man.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhaṃ pitṛsamaṃ cāpi bhrātaraṃ yo 'vamanyate so 'pi mṛtyum upāgamya krauñcayonau prajāyate
english: He who despises an elder brother, who is the equal of a father—that one too, having met his death, is reborn into the womb of a curlew.

sanskrit: krauñco jīvati māsāṃs tu daśa dvau sapta pañca ca tato nidhanam āpanno mānuṣatvam upāśnute
english: As a curlew he lives ten months, two, seven, and five; and meeting his death thereafter, he attains the state of a man.

sanskrit: vṛṣalo brāhmaṇīṃ gatvā kṛmiyonau prajāyate tatrāpatyaṃ samutpādya tato jāyati mūṣakaḥ
english: A low-born man who consorts with a brāhmaṇa woman is reborn into the womb of a worm; and having there begotten offspring, he is afterwards born a rat.

sanskrit: kṛtaghnas tu mṛto rājan yamasya viṣayaṃ gataḥ yamasya viṣaye kruddhair vadhaṃ prāpnoti dāruṇam
english: But the ingrate, O king, when dead, passes into the realm of Yama; and in Yama's realm he suffers a fearful slaughter at the hands of the wrathful.

sanskrit: paṭṭisaṃ mudgaraṃ śūlam agnikumbhaṃ ca dāruṇam asipatravanaṃ ghoraṃ vālukāṃ kūṭaśālmalīm
english: The spiked club, the mallet, the spear, the dreadful cauldron of fire, the terrible Sword-Leaf Forest, the burning sands, and the thorny Śālmali tree—

sanskrit: etāś cānyāś ca bahvīḥ sa yamasya viṣayaṃ gataḥ yātanāḥ prāpya tatrogrās tato vadhyati bhārata
english: these and many other fierce torments he undergoes, having passed into Yama's realm; and there he is put to death, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃsāracakram āsādya kṛmiyonau prajāyate kṛmir bhavati varṣāṇi daśa pañca ca bhārata tato garbhaṃ samāsādya tatraiva mriyate śiśuḥ
english: Entering the wheel of transmigration, he is reborn into the womb of a worm; as a worm he lives fifteen years, O Bhārata; then, entering a womb, the infant dies there itself.

sanskrit: tato garbhaśatair jantur bahubhiḥ saṃprajāyate saṃsārāṃś ca bahūn gatvā tatas tiryak prajāyate
english: Thereafter the creature is born through many hundreds of wombs; and having passed through many rounds of rebirth, it is then born as a beast.

sanskrit: mṛto duḥkham anuprāpya bahuvarṣagaṇān iha apunarbhāvasaṃyuktas tataḥ kūrmaḥ prajāyate
english: Having met his death and undergone suffering here through many sequences of years, deprived of release from rebirth, he is then born a tortoise.

sanskrit: aśastraṃ puruṣaṃ hatvā saśastraḥ puruṣādhamaḥ arthārthī yadi vā vairī sa mṛto jāyate kharaḥ
english: The basest of men who, bearing weapons, slays an unarmed man—whether out of greed for wealth or out of enmity—when dead is born an ass.

sanskrit: kharo jīvati varṣe dve tataḥ śastreṇa vadhyate sa mṛto mṛgayonau tu nityodvigno 'bhijāyate
english: As an ass he lives two years and is then slain by a weapon; and he, once dead, is born into the womb of a deer, forever trembling in fear.

sanskrit: mṛgo vadhyati śastreṇa gate saṃvatsare tu saḥ hato mṛgas tato mīnaḥ so 'pi jālena badhyate
english: As a deer he is killed by a weapon when a year has passed; the slain deer then becomes a fish, and that too is caught in a net.

sanskrit: māse caturthe saṃprāpte śvāpadaḥ saṃprajāyate śvāpado daśa varṣāṇi dvīpī varṣāṇi pañca ca
english: When the fourth month has come, he is born a beast of prey; as a beast of prey ten years, and as a leopard five years.

sanskrit: tatas tu nidhanaṃ prāptaḥ kālaparyāyacoditaḥ adharmasya kṣayaṃ kṛtvā tato jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: Then, meeting his death, driven on by the turning of time, and having worked off his unrighteousness, after that he is born a man.

sanskrit: striyaṃ hatvā tu durbuddhir yamasya viṣayaṃ gataḥ bahūn kleśān samāsādya saṃsārāṃś caiva viṃśatim
english: The evil-minded man who slays a woman passes into the realm of Yama; having undergone many afflictions and twenty rounds of rebirth—

sanskrit: tataḥ paścān mahārāja kṛmiyonau prajāyate kṛmir viṃśativarṣāṇi bhūtvā jāyati mānuṣaḥ
english: thereafter, O great king, he is reborn into the womb of a worm; and having been a worm for twenty years, he is born a man.

sanskrit: bhojanaṃ corayitvā tu makṣikā jāyate naraḥ makṣikāsaṃghavaśago bahūn māsān bhavaty uta tataḥ pāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā mānuṣatvam avāpnute
english: Having stolen food, a man is born a fly; subject to a swarm of flies, he remains so for many months; then, having worked off his sin, he attains the state of a man.

sanskrit: vādyaṃ hṛtvā tu puruṣo maśakaḥ saṃprajāyate tathā piṇyākasaṃmiśram aśanaṃ corayen naraḥ sa jāyate babhrusamo dāruṇo mūṣako naraḥ
english: Having stolen a musical instrument, a man is born a mosquito; and the man who steals food mixed with oil-cake is born a dreadful rat, tawny like a mongoose.

sanskrit: lavaṇaṃ corayitvā tu cīrīvākaḥ prajāyate dadhi hṛtvā bakaś cāpi plavo matsyān asaṃskṛtān
english: Having stolen salt, one is born a cricket; having stolen curds, a heron; and a waterfowl, by stealing fish not dressed for cooking.

sanskrit: corayitvā payaś cāpi balākā saṃprajāyate yas tu corayate tailaṃ tailapāyī prajāyate corayitvā tu durbuddhir madhu daṃśaḥ prajāyate
english: And having stolen milk, one is born a crane; he who steals oil is born an oil-drinking insect; and the evil-minded man who steals honey is born a stinging fly.

sanskrit: ayo hṛtvā tu durbuddhir vāyaso jāyate naraḥ pāyasaṃ corayitvā tu tittiritvam avāpnute
english: Having stolen iron, the evil-minded man is born a crow; and having stolen rice-milk pudding, he attains the state of a partridge.

sanskrit: hṛtvā paiṣṭam apūpaṃ ca kumbholūkaḥ prajāyate phalaṃ vā mūlakaṃ hṛtvā apūpaṃ vā pipīlikaḥ
english: Having stolen a cake of flour, one is born a horned owl; and having stolen fruit, a root, or a cake, an ant.

sanskrit: kāṃsyaṃ hṛtvā tu durbuddhir hārīto jāyate naraḥ rājataṃ bhājanaṃ hṛtvā kapotaḥ saṃprajāyate
english: Having stolen a bronze vessel, the evil-minded man is born a green pigeon; and having stolen a silver vessel, he is born a dove.

sanskrit: hṛtvā tu kāñcanaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ kṛmiyonau prajāyate krauñcaḥ kārpāsikaṃ hṛtvā mṛto jāyati mānavaḥ
english: Having stolen a vessel of gold, one is reborn into the womb of a worm; having stolen cotton goods, one becomes a curlew, and when dead is born a man.

sanskrit: corayitvā naraḥ paṭṭaṃ tv āvikaṃ vāpi bhārata kṣaumaṃ ca vastram ādāya śaśo jantuḥ prajāyate
english: Having stolen silk cloth, or woolen cloth, O Bhārata, or having taken a garment of fine linen, the creature is born a hare.

sanskrit: varṇān hṛtvā tu puruṣo mṛto jāyati barhiṇaḥ hṛtvā raktāni vastrāṇi jāyate jīvajīvakaḥ
english: Having stolen dyes, a man, when dead, is born a peacock; and having stolen red garments, he is born a jīvajīvaka pheasant.

sanskrit: varṇakādīṃs tathā gandhāṃś corayitvā tu mānavaḥ chucchundaritvam āpnoti rājaṃl lobhaparāyaṇaḥ
english: And the man given over to greed who steals pigments, perfumes, and the like attains the state of a musk-shrew, O king.

sanskrit: viśvāsena tu nikṣiptaṃ yo nihnavati mānavaḥ sa gatāsur naras tādṛṅ matsyayonau prajāyate
english: The man who denies a deposit placed with him in trust—such a man, when his breath has departed, is reborn into the womb of a fish.

sanskrit: matsyayonim anuprāpya mṛto jāyati mānuṣaḥ mānuṣatvam anuprāpya kṣīṇāyur upapadyate
english: Having attained the womb of a fish, when dead he is born a man; and having attained the human state, he is one whose lifespan is short.

sanskrit: pāpāni tu naraḥ kṛtvā tiryag jāyati bhārata na cātmanaḥ pramāṇaṃ te dharmaṃ jānanti kiṃ cana
english: Having committed sins, a man is born a beast, O Bhārata; and such creatures have no measure of themselves, nor do they know anything of dharma.

sanskrit: ye pāpāni narāḥ kṛtvā nirasyanti vrataiḥ sadā sukhaduḥkhasamāyuktā vyādhitās te bhavanty uta
english: Those men who, having committed sins, ever cast them off by vows—they become mingled with both pleasure and pain, and afflicted with disease.

sanskrit: asaṃvāsāḥ prajāyante mlecchāś cāpi na saṃśayaḥ narāḥ pāpasamācārā lobhamohasamanvitāḥ
english: Men of sinful conduct, possessed by greed and delusion, are born outcasts beyond fellowship, and barbarians too—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: varjayanti ca pāpāni janmaprabhṛti ye narāḥ arogā rūpavantas te dhaninaś ca bhavanty uta
english: But those men who shun sins from their very birth become free of disease, fair of form, and wealthy as well.

sanskrit: striyo 'py etena kalpena kṛtvā pāpam avāpnuyuḥ eteṣām eva jantūnāṃ patnītvam upayānti tāḥ
english: Women too, by this same order, attain the fruit of the sin they commit; they come to be the mates of these very same creatures.

sanskrit: parasvaharaṇe doṣāḥ sarva eva prakīrtitāḥ etad vai leśamātreṇa kathitaṃ te mayānagha aparasmin kathāyoge bhūyaḥ śroṣyasi bhārata
english: The faults arising from seizing another's property have all been proclaimed; this I have told you, O sinless one, in but the briefest measure; on another occasion of discourse you shall hear of it again, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: etan mayā mahārāja brahmaṇo vadataḥ purā surarṣīṇāṃ śrutaṃ madhye pṛṣṭaś cāpi yathātatham
english: This, O great king, I once heard from Brahmā as he spoke in the midst of the divine sages, when he was questioned, exactly as it is.

sanskrit: mayāpi tava kārtsnyena yathāvad anuvarṇitam etac chrutvā mahārāja dharme kuru manaḥ sadā
english: And by me it has been recounted to you in full, just as it is; having heard this, O great king, set your mind ever upon dharma.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca adharmasya gatir brahman kathitā me tvayānagha dharmasya tu gatiṃ śrotum icchāmi vadatāṃ vara kṛtvā karmāṇi pāpāni kathaṃ yānti śubhāṃ gatim
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The course of unrighteousness, O holy one, you have recounted to me, O sinless one; but I wish to hear the course of righteousness, O best of speakers. After committing sinful deeds, how do men attain an auspicious destiny?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca kṛtvā pāpāni karmāṇi adharmavaśam āgataḥ manasā viparītena nirayaṃ pratipadyate
english: Bṛhaspati said: Having committed sinful deeds, fallen under the sway of unrighteousness, with a mind gone astray, a man passes into hell.

sanskrit: mohād adharmaṃ yaḥ kṛtvā punaḥ samanutapyate manaḥsamādhisaṃyukto na sa seveta duṣkṛtam
english: But he who, having committed unrighteousness through delusion, afterwards feels remorse, and is endowed with composure of mind, will not pursue evil deeds again.
